messages:
Alana: Quick heads-up — saw a latency regression on the serving path when routing Qwen-7B (head_dim=77) through the mixtral runtime. It falls back to SDPA/compat path; p95 ~2.3x higher than flash on aligned head dims. 

Mike: What churned? Is this new since the kernel selection tweak last week? Any raw numbers?

Alana: Repro on canary 2026-03-10. Distribution: avg seq_len 128, heavy KV-cache usage (chat workloads). KV hit ratio steady; no obvious cache misses. Perf-bot attached traces.

perf-bot: Profiling summary (canary-2026-03-10):
```
model=qwen-7b  head_dim=77  seq=128  batch=1  kv_cache=on
chosen_kernel: sdpa_cuda_fallback
fallback_reason: head_dim % 8 != 0 -> flash not selected
p50_latency: 48.2ms  (flash baseline = 20.9ms)
p95_latency: 162.1ms (flash baseline = 69.7ms)
kernel_switch_overhead: +6.4ms
kv_cache_copy_bytes: 4.1MiB
notes: mask pad path entered for multihead ops
```

Xiang: Interesting — fallback reason looks like our flash kernel requires head_dim % 8 == 0 (and often %16). Could also be mask alignment hitting slower codepath. Do we have any Vec/pack conversion logs? Any FP promotion?

Alana: No FP promotion logged. Repro command:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"qwen-7b","input":"Tell me a story","max_tokens":64}' \
  https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate?seq_len=128
```
Runtime config snippet (canary):
```
kernel_selection:
  prefer: [flash, triton]
  fallback: [sdpa]
kv_cache:
  pad_to_multiple_of: 0  # current default: no pad
```

Jen: Quick local experiment: remapped head_dim 77 -> padded to 80 in the adapter layer (no model change) and forced flash path — latency drops to within 1.1x of baseline. Outputs look bitwise-close on a few eval prompts. So padding/aligning KV buffers buys us flash performance.

Mike: Good find. So mitigations: 1) heuristic pad KV/cache buffers to 8 or 16 when model head_dim%8!=0 for architectures that support flash, 2) prefer Triton/optimized SDPA when batching patterns or seq len indicate better throughput, 3) long term: add model-specific kernel metadata (allowed alignments).

Xiang: Also check RoPE scaling interactions — odd head dims can change our mask offsets and lead to mask-pad codepath being used which is slower. Need test matrix across RoPE scale factors (1.0 vs 0.5/2.0) and seq lengths 32/128/512.

Alana: Agreed. Also noticed when batch_size>1 the continuous-batching allocator creates misaligned buffers more often — triggers fallback earlier. We should ensure batch pad aligns to 8 too.

Jen: I'll prototype a small runtime patch that: (A) pads KV buffers to nearest multiple of 8 when head_dim%8!=0 and runtime_policy.prefers_flash==true, (B) adds a telemetry tag so we can filter by model and head_dim. Will run perf CI across our benchmark suite.

Mike: Add one caveat — padding increases memory and might affect Dedicated capacity packing. Keep patch opt-in behind a feature flag for now. Also add correctness tests (logits diff < 1e-5).

Alana: Filed INF-4823 with repro steps and initial perf traces, assigning to Jen. Plan: canary patch next week, run A/B against baseline for 72h, rollback if quality delta > threshold.

perf-bot: Scheduled benchmark INF-bench-1998765432: queued. Expected runs: qwen-7b head_dim {77,80,96} x seq_len {32,128,512} x kv_cache {on,off} x batch {1,4}.

Xiang: Also propose adding kernel selection rule: if (head_dim%8!=0 && model in {mixtral,llama,qwen}) then try pad->flash before falling back to sdpa. Less intrusive than changing global fallback order.

Jen: On it. Will push PR with toggle and perf CI logs. If perf looks good, we flip the flag in canary lanes then roll to prod.

Mike: Nice. Thanks all. Keep notes here and paste perf summary when CI completes. :thumbsup:
